title: A GIS – based method for assessment and mapping of noise pollution in Ota metropolis, Nigeria
author: Oyedepo, Adeyemi, et al.

steps.title: Calibrate sound level meter
steps.instruction: Use the internal calibrator to calibrate the precision‑grade sound‑level meter (IEC 651, ANSI S1.4 type 2) equipped with a ½‑in condenser microphone, 0.33‑octave filter, frequency range 31.5 Hz–8 kHz and level range 35–130 dB, before measurements at each selected site.

steps.title: Measure ambient noise at each location
steps.instruction: At each of the 41 street‑level sites (road junctions, market centres, passenger loading parks, residential areas) hold the meter comfortably, point the microphone toward the suspected source at >1 m from any reflecting object, and record A‑weighted instantaneous sound pressure level (LAi) every 30 s for 30 min (60 readings). Repeat the 30‑min recording for three periods: morning 07:00–09:00, afternoon 14:00–16:00, and evening 18:00–20:00.

steps.title: Record traffic and environmental data
steps.instruction: While measuring, count and log the number of cars, tricycles, motorcycles and trucks passing the point, note the prevailing environmental conditions, and record the GPS coordinates of the sampling point.

steps.title: Calculate noise descriptors and indices
steps.instruction: Using the recorded LAi values, compute the following descriptors for each location and time: L10, L90, LAeq, LD, LN, TNI, LNP, NC, and NEI according to the formulas: LAeq = 10 log10 (1/N ∑ Antilog(LAi10)), LD = 10 log10 [½ (Antilog(LAeq(m))10 + Antilog(LAeq(A))10)], LN = 10 log10 [½ (Antilog(LAeq(E))10 + Antilog(LAeq(N))10)], TNI = 4 × (L10 – L90) + (L90 – 30) dB(A), LNP = Leq + a(L10 – L90), NC = (L10 – L90), NEI = Σ (ti/Ti).
